description: Use this when someone reads or prints a scale drawing or floor plan and asks what a measurement on paper means in real life, or which scale or sheet size to use. Converts lengths on a scale drawing. With a scale 1:N and a length on paper it gives the real length; with a scale and a real length it gives the length on paper; with a length on paper and the real length it shows, and no scale, it finds N. It also gives the nearest common scale in each system, metric (ISO 5455, 1:5 to 1:2500), US architectural (3" = 1'-0" to 1/32" = 1'-0", N = 12 ÷ inches per foot) and US engineering (1" = 10'-0" to 1" = 100'-0", N = 12 × feet per inch), with the difference as a fraction. For a plan size it gives the plan's size on paper and the smallest ISO sheet (A4 to A0) and US sheet (Letter, ARCH A, Tabloid, ARCH B to ARCH E) that holds it inside the margins, upright or turned.

margin.description: Clear margin on every edge of the sheet, in millimeters; 10 when it is missing.

paper.description: A length measured on the drawing, in millimeters.

plan.description: Size of the whole plan, for the smallest sheet it fits on.

prefixItems.description: Width of the whole plan in the building, in millimeters.
Depth of the whole plan in the building, in millimeters.

real.description: A length in the building, in millimeters.

scale.description: The N of the drawing scale 1:N, such as 50 for 1:50 or 48 for 1/4" = 1'-0". Leave it out to find N from paper and real.
